'''''Barbula unguiculata''''', also called as '''Bird's-claw Beard-moss''' is a species of [[moss]] belonging to the family [[Pottiaceae]].<ref name="worldfloraonline.org">{{cite web |title=Barbula unguiculata Hedw. |url=http://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0001153324 |website=www.worldfloraonline.org |access-date=28 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Qian |first=Hong |url=https://www.google.co.kr/books/edition/Plants_of_British_Columbia/cBciWJHM5GkC?hl=ko&gbpv=1&dq=Barbula+unguiculata&pg=PA207&printsec=frontcover |title=Plants of British Columbia: Scientific and Common Names of Vascular Plants, Bryophytes, and Lichens |last2=Klinka |first2=K. |date=1998 |publisher=UBC Press |isbn=978-0-7748-0652-7 |language=en}}</ref> Its color is usually distinctive, a kind of bright yellow-green shared by few similar acrocarps such as ''[[Trichostomum]]'' species. Its [[leaves]] always look opaque, thanks to its densely [[Papillose|papillose leaf cells]]. In dry conditions, the leaves frequently twist or curl around the stem, whereas they spread outward when moist.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Barbula unguiculata - British Bryological Society |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/barbula-unguiculata/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616151613/https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/barbula-unguiculata/ |archive-date=2025-06-16 |access-date=2025-10-16 |work=British Bryological Society |language=en-GB}}</ref> Each [[leaf]] is parallel-sided for most of its lengths.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bird's-claw beard-moss – Barbula unguiculata |url=https://www.naturespot.org.uk/species/birds-claw-beard-moss |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=NatureSpot}}</ref>

The stems of Barbula unguiculata typically reach lengths of approximately {{Convert|1 to 2|mm|in}}, while the [[Leaf|leaves]] generally measure between {{Convert|1 and 2.5|mm|in}} in length. The [[seta]] of Barbula unguiculata is {{Convert|1 to 2.5|cm|in}}, and the [[Spore|spores]] are 8 to 11 [[Micrometre|μm]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Bryophyte Portal - Barbula unguiculata |url=https://bryophyteportal.org/portal/taxa/index.php?taxon=Barbula+unguiculata&formsubmit=Search+Terms |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=bryophyteportal.org}}</ref> Capsules mature in winter and early spring, occasionally summer or fall.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Webmaster |first=David Ratz |title=Bird's-claw Beard Moss - Montana Field Guide |url=https://fieldguide.mt.gov/speciesDetail.aspx?elcode=NBMUS0Q0K0 |access-date=2025-11-01 |website=fieldguide.mt.gov |language=en}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
Barbula unguiculata typically colonizes open, exposed and disturbed sites, on [[soil]], [[sand]], [[gravel]], [[sandstone]], [[granite]], [[limestone]], [[Wall|walls]], [[Road cuts|roadcuts]], paths, [[Lawn|lawns]], [[Ditch|ditches]], [[Boulder|boulders]], and cliff crevices, and low to high elevations (50-2700 m). It is frequently found on  eutrophic grounds, such as [[Sidewalk|sidewalks]] and [[Arable field|arable fields]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Barbula unguiculata |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/barbula-unguiculata/ |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=British Bryological Society}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=moss-Barbula unguiculata – Ohio Moss and Lichen Association |url=https://ohiomosslichen.org/moss-barbula-unguiculata/ |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=ohiomosslichen.org}}</ref>

== Habitat ==
''Barbula unguiculata'' is known to be able to use [[artificial light]] to grow in places which are otherwise devoid of natural light, such as [[Niagara Cave]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Thatcher |first1=Edward P. |date=1947 |title=Observations on Bryophytes Living in an Artificially Illuminated Limestone Cave |journal=The American Midland Naturalist |volume=37 |issue=3 |pages=797–800 |doi=10.2307/2421476}}</ref> and [[Crystal Cave (Wisconsin)|Crystal Cave]] in [[Wisconsin]].<ref name="Thatcher 1949">{{cite journal |last1=Thatcher |first1=Edward P. |date=1949 |title=Bryophytes of an Artificially Illuminated Cave |journal=The Bryologist |volume=52 |issue=4 |pages=212–214 |doi=10.2307/3239480}}</ref> Barbula unguiculata is common in eastern [[North America]], [[Asia]], and [[Europe]], and elsewhere in the North and [[South temperate zone|South Temperate zones]]. It is rare in the [[tropics]].<ref name=":1" />
